How Claude Uses Context

Claude reads your context, then writes from it.
CONTEXT
Your prompt
Conversation
Instructions
Files and data
→
MODEL
Reads everything you gave it
Predicts the next word
Repeats until done
→
OUTPUT
A LinkedIn post
A content plan
An analysis
Same model. Different context. Different result.

What Counts as Context

Your prompt is one piece. Claude reads four.
01 Request
The one line you typed. For example: write a post about our first meetup.
02 Conversation
Everything you already said in this chat.
03 Instructions
Strategy, voice and rules you want it to follow.
04 Files and data
Documents and connected apps, like Notion.
You wrote one line. Claude used four layers.

Why More Isn’t Better

Irrelevant context makes the useful part harder to find.
Everything you have
Dump it all in
✗Long chat history
✗Every file and old draft
✗The whole knowledge base
Fills the window. Costs more. Buries what matters.
→
What this task needs
Only the relevant part
✓The current request
✓Strategy and voice
✓A few good examples
Focused and easier to use.
The goal is not maximum context. It is the right context.

Tokens

The unit AI uses to measure text. More tokens fill the window and cost more.
INPUT
Your prompt
Plus all context
→
MODEL
Processes tokens
Both in and out
→
OUTPUT
The generated response
Rule of thumb: 1,000 tokens is roughly 600–750 English words.

Choosing a Model

Match the model to the task: speed, depth and cost.
Haiku
FASTEST
Quick, simple tasks.
Sonnet
FAST AND SMART
Everyday work, with the best mix of speed and intelligence.
Opus
KNOWLEDGE WORK
Long, multi-step knowledge work.
Fable
DEMANDING REASONING
Long projects and heavy reasoning. Slower, higher cost.
EFFORT
How much work Claude puts into an answer, from quick to thorough.
LOW→MEDIUM→HIGH→EXTRA HIGH→MAX
Routine tasks. Uses less of your limit.Deepest thinking. Slower, uses more of your limit.

Why Skills

A skill remembers what to use and how, so you never re-explain it.
Without a skill
name the files, explain the steps
Read about-me.md, audience.md and voice.md. Write two posts in my format. Check every voice rule. Now write one about our first meetup.
✗ You supply the files and the steps
With a skill
one line, everything included
Write a post about our first meetup.
✓ Claude supplies the files and the steps
Say it once. Reuse it every time.

From a prompt to a skill.

A skill is a .md file with a name and a description that Claude can run. It reads the same brain you just built.
--- name: resource-analysis description: Audit competitors against a scoring framework, populate a Notion database. --- When I ask to analyse competitors: 1. Read about-me.md and voice.md for who we are. 2. Score each competitor 1 to 5 against the framework. 3. Populate a Notion database.

The Feedback Loop

Every pick and every reason makes the next post better.
1 Generate
The skill writes posts and saves them to Notion.
→
2 Human in the loop
You mark each post Approved, Rejected or Rewritten, and say why.
→
3 Save
Claude saves your feedback and reasons in feedback.md.
→
4 Use
Next time, the skill reads feedback.md before writing.
The skill learns from files, not from chat.

Homework

You already built your two core files.

about-me.md
Who you are, real numbers, who you help, what you want to be known for. Rule at the top: only real facts - if one is missing, leave a gap and ask.
voice.md
Your three words, your exact reader, phrases you use, phrases you never use, your contrarian take. This is the fix for output that sounds like everyone else.
about-me gives Claude the facts. brand-voice gives it the sound. Together, that is your brain.

Start simple. Branch as you grow.

Core files
about-me.md
Who you are, what you do, why it matters. Claude reads this first to understand the brand.
voice.md
Tone, banned phrases, post structure, examples of good vs bad. Makes every post sound like you.
strategy.md
Pillars, audience, goals, posting rhythm. The strategic layer every piece of content is checked against.

Chapter 4 · Make It Yours
Chapter 4 · Make It Yours

What each branch file does.

from about-me
story-bank.md
A list of real moments Claude can draw on so posts feel lived-in, not made up.
milestones.md
Key dates, wins, pivots. Lets Claude write milestone posts without needing the history each time.
social-proof.md
Real quotes and results. Claude uses these in testimonial and community posts.
from voice
hooks.md
10-20 approved opening lines. Claude uses them as templates, not copies. Stops generic openers.
post-formats.md
Named structures like before/after or session recap. Claude picks the right format per idea.
cta-bank.md
Pre-approved CTAs by goal (sign up, share, comment). Every post ends on a single, sharp ask.
from strategy
icp-details.md
Expanded ICP profiles with real job titles, pains, language they use. Makes targeting more precise.
seasonal-topics.md
Time-sensitive topics by month. Events, launches, recurring moments. Anchors the content calendar.

What a good .md file looks like.

voice.md
# Brand voice How I sound. Claude reads this before writing anything. ## Three words Direct, warm, practical. ## Who I write for Non-technical founders in Berlin, 28 to 42, behind on AI. ## Words I never use "unlock", "game-changer", em dashes.
Title - what the file is.
One-line purpose - why Claude reads it.
Sections Claude can act on - real, specific answers, not vague labels.
Vague answers give vague output. Every line has to be something Claude can use.
